items.title: US says sanctions will 'squash' Iran's economy and 'collapse' its regime
items.description: The US treasury secretary says allies will need to decide whether they "are with us or against us".

items.title: UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada condemn Israel's West Bank settlement project
items.description: European countries and Canada pile on pressure over Israel's plans to expand settlements in a strategically vital part of the occupied West Bank.

items.title: Russia 'purposefully' hit critical infrastructure in latest strikes, Kyiv mayor says
items.description: At least 17 people were killed in the "massive attack" overnight on Ukraine's capital, as mayor Vitali Klitschko warns hot water supply has been disrupted.

items.title: Founder of collapsed Chinese property giant Evergrande sentenced to life in prison
items.description: Hui's sentencing marks a key moment in the fallout from Evergrande's collapse, which shook China's property sector.

items.title: Como mayor bans 'beasts' in city centre after being hit by bike
items.description: Alessandro Rapinese issues the prohibition for the historic city centre after an encounter with a cyclist last month.

items.title: Assad officer extradited to Syria on war crimes charges for first time
items.description: Lebanon handed over former General Adel Issa, as Syria steps up its pursuit of wanted members of the former regime.

items.title: Giant whales move into Greenland waters as ice disappears
items.description: Melting sea ice from climate change has opened up the region for giant whales to undertake "feeding frenzies".

items.title: German neo-Nazi suspected of deadly 1970 fire at Jewish retirement home
items.description: Investigators believe they have identified an arsonist who attacked a Jewish community centre in Munich in 1970, killing seven people.

items.title: Ex-Zambian minister killed in security raid on opposition
items.description: Police confirm Mutotwe Kafwaya's death after growing demands for information about his whereabouts.

items.title: Togo charges two French journalists over incorrect documents, rights group says
items.description: Gaël Mocaër and Sebastian Perez Pezzani's detention is "unjustified and disproportionate", Reporters Without Borders says.

items.title: Landslide at unlicensed Colombian gold mine kills 13
items.description: Four members of an indigenous family are among the dead, witnesses said.

items.title: Mushroom killer must stay in jail forever for 'truly dreadful' crime, appeal court told
items.description: Prosecutors say Erin Patterson's sentence was "manifestly inadequate" as it allows for the possibility of parole.

items.title: Israel confirms soldiers fired at car in which Hind Rajab was killed and opens criminal investigation
items.description: The five-year-old Palestinian girl initially survived the attack and pleaded for help but her body was recovered later with those of six of her relatives.

items.title: Missing teen hiker found dead in Australian bush after eight-day search
items.description: The state premier initially said Lily Hooper had been found alive before police confirmed her death.

items.title: Former Liberian vice-president charged in drug-trafficking probe
items.description: Jewel Howard-Taylor was arrested at Liberia's international airport and has not commented on the allegations.

items.title: Australia 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open criminal investigation into killing of aid worker in Gaza
items.description: Australia's foreign minister summoned the Israeli ambassador over "insulting" Zomi Frankcom decision.

items.title: Canadian marathon route was 674m too long
items.description: Organisers of the Edmonton Marathon admit their course this year was more than half a kilometre too long.

items.title: Four workers dead after being hit by train in Japan
items.description: The train collided with the four men at Shin-Kanuma Station, north of Tokyo, authorities say.

items.title: Captured Ukrainian-born soldiers tell BBC why they fought for Russia
items.description: Men born in Ukraine who fought for Russia are tried for treason, but at a prisoner of war camp in western Ukraine, many believe they were defending their homeland.

items.title: Key Trump aide Natalie Harp suddenly in spotlight after years behind scenes
items.description: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff used a speech to note the closeness of one aide to the president.
